messages:
ajay: heads up — getting multiple reports from support about p95 API latency from eu-west users starting ~03:40 UTC. spikes look TLS-heavy (handshake time + retransmits). ticket C-3492 attached.

oncall-bot: ALERT: routing-p95-eu-west spike detected. metric: api.latency.p95 = 980ms (baseline 120ms). affected pops: eu-west-1, eu-west-2.

support: customers A/B/C seeing slow completions, some timeouts. screenshots + HAR uploaded to ticket. says recent deploys? unsure. :frowning:

maria: copying telemetry — is this correlated with any egress peering change or GSLB weight tweak? I don't see recent deploys in last hour.

ajay: no deploys. I ran quick probes from our probe fleet and one customer region:
```
# from eu-probe-12
$ dig +short api.redwood.io @8.8.8.8
52.31.12.7
$ traceroute -n 52.31.12.7
  1  10.0.0.1
  2  198.51.100.1
  3  203.0.113.5
  4  52.31.12.7
$ curl -v --max-time 5 https://api.redwood.io/health
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLS handshake took 0.68s
* HTTP/2 200
```
handshake in probe ~680ms vs baseline ~80-120ms.

cheng: ran tcpdump on edge for a few flows — seeing repeated SYN retransmits to backend egress IPs and occasional SNI mismatch logs (server rejected early data?). snippets: `tls: handshake failed: no certificate for sni \"api.redwood.io\"` but only for ~0.4% of flows.

devin: could be route churn at CDN/GSLB causing cross-az hairpin or BGP flap transiently selecting longer path. Can you paste the BGP/route-change logs for eu pops?

ajay: grabbing route change window 03:35–03:50. quick grep shows a handful of origin AS path changes and an AS prepending event for a peering we use in eu-west-2.

maria: that matches support times. mitigation options: 1) pin customers to nearest pop (quick config) 2) reduce GSLB weight on the problematic POP 3) enable fallback to dedicated lower-latency variant (if available). which is lowest-risk now?

devin: lowest-risk is adjusting GSLB weight away from eu-west-2 for 10m and monitor. I can push weight change. also enable additional TCP retries on the edge for 1m while we observe (helps SYN losses).

cheng: we should also rotate the TLS cert on the affected edge box if SNI mismatch persists. but that's heavier.

ajay: i'll coordinate with netops for weight change. applying now.

oncall-bot: ACTION: devin initiated GSLB weight adjustment away from eu-west-2 -> new weight 10% (was 60%). notified at 03:55:10 UTC.

ajay: after weight shift, p95 dropped to ~180ms within 2 minutes for incoming probe traffic. support confirmed two customers improved. still seeing a small set of flows with TLS handshake 400–600ms.

maria: can we add a short-term runbook note to ticket C-3492: GSLB weight rollback if error rate >1% or p95 >500ms? Also capture traceroutes+tcpdumps for those persistent flows.

devin: good. i'll hold the weight change for 20 minutes then slowly reintroduce. next steps: netops to review peering prepends, infra to check TLS config drift on eu-pop images, support to escalate any remaining customer timeouts.

ajay: I'll attach the probe traces and tcpdumps to the ticket and mark triage done. followups: netops post-mortem + potential peering SLA check. thanks all. :thumbsup:
